question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{3}+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & \frac{x}{3}+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our two equations for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{3} & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & \frac{x}{3} & =\frac{2\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{3} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & \frac{x}{3} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+6n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{3\pi }{2}+6n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{12n\pi }{2} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{3\pi }{2}+\frac{12n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(12n+1)\pi }{2} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(12n+3)\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\frac{3\pi }{2}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions are: 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{2},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{3\pi }{2}
$$
